item.title: Kathleen Ryan (nee McCabe)

item.title: Bats' roost would be destroyed if supermarket gets go ahead, according to report
item.description: A roost for five bats will be destroyed if planning permission is granted for an Aldi store in Boyle. But the supermarket chain says it will take action to ensure they aren't significantly impacted. A badger's den was also found on the site, and badgers are a protected species. Aldi wants to build a supermarket and refurbish five houses in Patrick Street in Boyle. The council looked for more information before deciding whether to give planning permission. item.title: Jesus knew what it was like to be a refugee and homeless, says local Reverend
item.description: A local Church of Ireland rector says Jesus knew what it was like to be homeless and a refugee. Reverend Canon Simon Scott oversees the Longford group of parishes. He says Christmas is a great reminder of something incredible - that God loves us so much that he came down among us. He says God is still among us and had his own vulnerabilities: Advertisement

item.title: ALONE will deliver over 2,000 Christmas dinners to older people
item.description: ALONE will deliver over 2,000 Christmas dinners tomorrow, reflecting the growing need for support among older people this year. The charity says Ireland’s aging population is driving demand for its services. Today, nearly 200,000 older people live by themselves, with ALONE supporting around two thirds of them. CEO Seán Moynihan says older people face so many challenges in modern society: Advertisement

item.title: Over 25,000 local NCT failures so far this year
item.description: Over 25,000 cars failed the NCT in the Shannonside region in the first eleven months of this year. The statistics were made available on the official NCT website. Just over 45,000 tests were carried out in Carrick-on-Shannon, Castlerea and Longford between January and November. Advertisement Castlerea had the highest pass rate in the region at 45.46%. That was followed by Carrick-on-Shannon at 44.75% and Longford at 41.67%. Across all three centres there were over 3,782 dangerous failures. Adver

item.title: Check in on vulnerable people over Christmas - Boyle activist
item.description: People are being urged to check in on vulnerable people over Christmas. Boyle's Jane Suffin says a lot of people are lonely over the festive period, especially in rural areas. She's encouraging people to keep an eye on them: Advertisement

item.title: Utter Madness if Bats Scrupper Boyle's Aldi - Crosby
item.description: The discovery of bats on the site of a proposed Aldi supermarket in Roscommon shouldn't be a 'death knell' for the project. That's according to local Fianna Fáil councillor Sean Moylan, who says the result of an Ecological Assesment was a setback. Aldi wants to build the supermarket and refurbish five houses on Patrick Street in Boyle. Advertisement Roscommon County Council had sought more information before making a decision. item.title: Free Christmas dinner event in Boyle on December 28th
item.description: A free Christmas dinner event in Boyle is running for its ninth year this weekend. The annual get-together in King House Tea Rooms will take place on Sunday, December 28th at 1pm. A three-course meal will be served, followed by music and entertainment. Advertisement Walk-ins are welcome but the public is advised to ring directly to book a space. Dorothy Shannon from King House Tea Rooms says the aim is to ensure nobody feels alone this festive season: Advertisement

item.title: Local Patients Among 1,500 Waiting Over an Hour for Ambulances
item.description: It's emerged that patients locally were among fifteen-hundred that waited more than an hour for an ambulance in the first half of this year. According to National Ambulance Service figures, 365 of these delayed responses occurred in the region covering Leitrim and Roscommon. Earlier this year, 52-year-old Drumshanbo resident had to wait an hour and twenty minutes for an ambulance to arrive after having suffered from a stroke. item.title: 24 New Speed Camera Zones Aim to Curb Local Speeding
item.description: It's hoped that the introduction of 24 new speed camera zones will see a crackdown on speeding locally. Gardaí announced the new measures yesterday, with 15 to be allocated in Roscommon. There will be six in Leitrim, while Longford will have three with one more community request, Advertisement The primary purpose of safety cameras is to reduce speed-related collisions, lessen injuries and save lives on Irish roads.
